head: f3c25eb
emphasis: availability, resource exhaustion, and integrity of the SLO signal
transcription_reason: GI-011 — pre-write-gate.js normalises .claude/worktrees/<id>/specs/reviews/... and fails to match its own specs/reviews/** allow-entry, so this instance could not write its own artifacts. It declined to bypass the gate and reported inline instead. Findings below are transcribed verbatim in substance from its final report; the measurements are its own.

findings.description: A real p95 breach is masked by anonymous scrapes. record_request excludes /metrics from _request_counts but still calls observe_duration unconditionally, so every anonymous scrape feeds a fast observation into the global histogram. Measured: 40x /slow at ~900 ms gave a real p95 of 975.0 ms (BREACH vs the 500 ms budget); then 2,000 anonymous GET /metrics in 2.3 s drove the reported p95 to 4.8 ms (PASS), computed with the project's own prom-parse.js histogramP95. errorRate read 0.0000% both times, so the masking left ZERO trace in http_requests_total. Excluding /metrics from its own counters made the signal harder to reason about: it removed the audit trail of scrape volume while leaving the scrape's effect on p95 fully intact.
findings.fix: Apply _SLI_EXCLUDED_ROUTES to observe_duration as well, or filter per-route in the consumer.

findings.description: SEC3-003 residual: a real 50% outage still passes the 1% budget. 50 real 500s + 50 200s gave errorRate 50.0000% (correct breach); adding 20,000 anonymous GET /health drove it to 0.2488% (PASS). The /metrics exclusion is irrelevant because /health dilutes identically; only ~4,900 extra requests are needed to push 50 errors under 1%. f3c25eb is a partial fix at best. Root defect is global lifetime summation with no per-route dimension at .claude/hooks/lib/prom-parse.js:37-47 — out-of-scope harness code.
findings.fix: Per-route SLI aggregation in the consumer; rate-limit and/or authenticate /metrics.

findings.description: Frontend Money accepts unbounded magnitude and format() OOM-crashes V8. Money.fromWire("1e20000000") parses in 0.0 ms; format() takes 1,888 ms and yields a 26.7 MB string. fromWire("1e400000000") produces FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit, exit 134 — from an 11-byte input. Not reachable today: the frontend has 2 source files, no fetch/router/ingress, and MoneyText has no non-test caller. Asymmetry: the backend rejects >1e25 in 0.0 ms; the frontend has no bound at all.
findings.fix: Bound the exponent in toQuantizedDecimal to match the backend.

findings.description: X-Request-ID is unvalidated, unbounded and structurally un-scrubbable. A 1,000,000-byte id is accepted, reflected verbatim and logged verbatim. 4111111111111111 appears raw as "request_id": "4111111111111111" because JSONLogFormatter injects request_id AFTER RedactionFilter runs (config/logging.py:183), so no registered value can ever scrub it. Refuted sub-claims, measured: log amplification is 1.00x (1,000,040 B in, 1,000,147 B logged) so it is not an amplification DoS; CRLF header-splitting fails (the parser drops the injected header); raw control chars get 400; JSON line integrity holds against quote/backslash/json-ish ids (1 line, parses, level not forged).
findings.fix: Bound length and charset, regenerate on validation failure, and scrub in the formatter.

findings.description: decimal.Overflow escapes Money.multiply. _quantize at :71-76 catches only InvalidOperation. Money("1.00").multiply(Decimal("1e1000000")) raises uncaught decimal.Overflow in 0.00 ms. Still exactly a contract break (500 instead of 422), not a DoS — confirmed. Siblings swept clean: add, subtract, __eq__, __hash__ and multiply(int 10) are all safe because quantize bounds every Money below 1e26. Round-2 timing dispute resolved — both instances were right about different scalars: multiply(Decimal) is 0.00 ms, but multiply(10**1000000) is 9,538 ms, of which 9,531 ms is CPython's int-to-Decimal coercion, not the multiplication (94.81 ms at 10**100000 scaling to 9,530.95 ms at 10**1000000 — quadratic). Unreachable: multiply has zero call sites in backend/src.
findings.fix: Catch ArithmeticError; bound the scalar's digit count.

findings.description: Host-header-reflected redirect. GET /health/ with Host: evil.example returns 307 with Location: http://evil.example/health. Not a classic open redirect (it needs a cache or proxy in front to matter), but no TrustedHostMiddleware exists.

No security response headers at all — /health returns only date, server, content-length, content-type, x-request-id; no CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options or HSTS. /docs and /openapi.json return anonymous 200. Low now: no server-side HTML templating and no user content rendered.
findings.fix: Add a security-headers middleware when the first UI route lands.

findings.description: PII redaction is inert — register_sensitive/redact_values have zero production call sites outside logging.py's own definitions; ba457bf added them to specs only. So _scrub never receives values, the lru_cache(256) PII-key retention never populates, and every bypass variant is latent (_SEPARATOR_RUN tolerates only space/tab/hyphen, so dot, underscore, NBSP, zero-width, homoglyph and NFKC forms all defeat it). Do not read this as a passing control; it becomes high the moment E1-S1 lands an origination route.
findings.fix: Wire register_sensitive at the call sites that introduce PII, and normalise before matching.

findings.description: Declared money wire pattern is not enforced. _WIRE_PATTERN lives only in the JSON schema; no_info_plain_validator_function bypasses Pydantic string validation, so _validate_money accepts "12.3", "1e6", "  12.00  ", "1_000.00" and "-0.005" against a documented ^-?\d+\.\d{2}$. Parse-cost DoS refuted: a 4,000,000-character digit string is rejected in 31.3 ms (linear).
findings.fix: Apply the pattern in the validator, or narrow the declared schema to the tolerance actually implemented.

findings.description: Money's magnitude bound is an artifact of ambient mutable global state, not an invariant: decimal context prec=28 accepts 1e25, prec=60 accepts 1e26, prec=200 accepts 1e100. Money never uses localcontext. Note the is_finite() guard was written as if Overflow were untrapped — untrapped, multiply returns Infinity and is caught correctly, which is why SEC4-005 exists only under the default trapping context.
findings.fix: Wrap arithmetic in an explicit localcontext with a pinned precision.

findings.description: seen/_observe hygiene. An app sending 100,000 response starts grows seen to 100,000 ints for one request, but only one request is counted (seen[0]) — no double-count on any path that could be constructed, and growth is app-driven rather than attacker- or slow-client-driven. The 500 default is REFUTED as an attacker vector: 5 curl --max-time 1 aborts against a 5 s handler on the live server recorded 6 x /slow status=200 and zero 5xx — uvicorn does not cancel the handler on client disconnect. Injected directly at the ASGI layer, CancelledError does record 500, but no client-reachable path produces it. Caveat: verified for uvicorn's default httptools implementation only.
findings.fix: None required for security; see the code-review axis for the design finding.

remediation_verified_closed: B-4/CR-304 quadratic format(): old regex 59/254/1,015/4,102 ms at 12.5k/25k/50k/100k digits (clean 4x per doubling, matching round 3's 4,091 ms); new walk 1.0/0.6/1.6/3.6 ms (linear), 1,149x faster at 100k. Real Money.format() across 5 doublings 12.5k->400k: 1.6/1.8/3.8/8.9/16.4/51.5 ms, flat at 0.07-0.13 us per 1k digits. Output byte-identical to the old regex for n=1..60.
CR-301 method cardinality bounded: PROPFIND -> method="<other>"; FROBNICATE, GET1 and lowercase get get 400 BELOW the ASGI layer. Two distinct method labels after hostile traffic.
B-2 route cardinality bounded: 300 unique random paths -> one route="<unmatched>" series, count 302; whole exposition 78 lines.

B-1 label injection closed: quote/brace and CRLF path payloads -> 404, zero forged series. Reachability is closed by the LABEL BOUNDING (both labels are closed sets), not by the escaping — \r remains absent from _LABEL_ESCAPES (routes.py:78), which is harmless only while no attacker-controlled string reaches a label.

unscanned_classes.secrets: gitleaks unprovisioned — UNSCANNED, not clean. settings.py manually confirmed env-sourced with a TRUELEND_ prefix, no hardcoded credentials and no debug flag, but the changed set was not machine-scanned.
unscanned_classes.sast: semgrep unprovisioned — UNSCANNED. Injection coverage is manual and dynamic only. No SQL/ORM/template/shell sink exists in the changed set (no DB layer, no HTML templating, no subprocess), so residual risk is low but unscanned.
unscanned_classes.python_dependency_cve: pip-audit unprovisioned; backend/uv.lock was not audited.
unscanned_classes.js_dependency_cve: Carried forward unverified by this instance: 1 critical (vitest) + 1 high (vite), devDependency-only, absent from any production image.
unscanned_classes.note: The clean security-scan.json was not treated as evidence at any point.
